title: TrustLayer Remediation Guidance Catalog
description: Machine-readable guidance for closing a compliance gap. Guidance is data, not code: a regulation changes far more often than a planner does, and a catalog can be reviewed by someone who does not read Python. Every entry states its legal basis, the dimension of work it belongs to (technical / documentation / process), and how to verify it is actually done.

version.description: Catalog version, independent of the control framework's.

jurisdiction.description: Legal jurisdiction, so guidance written for the EU is not silently applied elsewhere.

$defs_note.description: Reserved for catalog authors' notes; ignored by the planner.

id.description: Stable identifier. Cited in generated plans so a plan can be traced back to the guidance that produced it.

title.description: Imperative summary of the action, e.g. 'Classify the system against Annex III'.

dimension.description: technical = code, configuration or instrumentation; documentation = an artifact a reader or auditor consumes; process = a recurring human activity with an owner and a cadence. A gap closed in the wrong dimension is the most common failure: writing a policy document does not create the process that executes it.

applies_to.description: When this guidance fires. At least one selector is required; an entry that matches nothing is a catalog authoring error, not a silent no-op.

control_ids.description: Control identifiers from the framework catalog (evidence_linker).

statuses.description: Statuses this guidance responds to. Omitted means every non-passing status. 'PASS' is deliberately not permitted: guidance for something already satisfied is noise that buries the real work.

legal_basis.description: Article and annex references, e.g. ['Art. 9(2)', 'Annex IV(5)']. Present so a reader can check the claim rather than trust it.

blocking.description: True when the gap blocks a conformity claim outright, as opposed to weakening it. Drives ordering.

effort.description: S = under a day; M = days; L = weeks or a standing commitment. An estimate for sequencing, never a quote.

owner_role.description: Who must act. Named because the single most common reason a gap stays open is that no role owned it.

why.description: What goes wrong if this is left open, in terms of the obligation. Not a restatement of the title.

steps.description: Ordered, concrete actions. Each should be executable by the named owner without further interpretation.

artifacts.description: Files this work creates or changes. Paths are suggestions for review — nothing is ever written automatically (design principle P4).

verification.description: How to demonstrate the gap is closed — ideally a command or an evidence query, not an assertion. Guidance with no verification step produces work nobody can confirm.

evidence_hint.description: Which runtime evidence would substantiate this control once the work is done, phrased for an evidence query author.

references.description: Links or citations for further reading.
